title: Greenville Pepper Shakers and Welch's own Texas band
summary: Welch played with the Greenville Pepper Shakers and led a seven-piece band, playing Louisiana clubs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: with two bands. I played with the Greenville Pepper Shakers and I played with the Texas Cernator. That was a band of my own. I had a seven-piece officer of my own by the name of the Texas Cernator. And where was that? That was in Tallulah, Louisiana. We left Vicksburg, Mississippi with a band. With seven pieces. We got together and made a band.
And what was your line up there?
Well, I had a trombone, sax, trumpet, clarinet, and a drum, guitar.
And can you tell me the names of some of those fellows?

Well, it's been quite a while now. I just about done forgot their names. About a couple of them. I know one boy. He's still playing. And I hear him over television sometimes playing. He was a white boy and he used to play with us. His name was Ted. Ted Williams is his name. But, uh...

His home was in, uh, in, uh, Cleveland, Mississippi. Mm-hmm. Well, he came to Greenville and got with us. And, uh, he asked us, would we see if we could scrap up a nice little band and make some dough. But we decided to scrap up. We went around and got boys and used to play in the band. They had quit. We went around and got together and made us a nice little orchestra. We used to play for Bob Knights up there, here in Louisiana. And, uh, we used to play at the River Road Inn. We played at Mr. Bob Knight's club. We played in St. Joe, Louisiana. We played for Mr. Ellie Coleman's daughter. She had a little, uh, little place out there. And she, we signed a contract to play for her. Other words, we was doing pretty good. So, the boys all split up and went back, went back north. And I wouldn't go with them, so... You know how I'd go, you know.
Yes, sir. I like the south, and so... Here's where I wind up. Oh, my God.
